answer.evidence: The bed body is a tall horizontal mattress area (rows 9-37). It has a pillow and sheet band, a green blanket, and a light front-edge line at row 36 with a darker line at rows 37-38. Below that is a footboard panel (rows 39-44) with a handle slot and short feet at rows 45-46, which forms a front face of more than 3 rows. The drawing is quite top-down, but the top surface and the front face are both present, so it reads as three_quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The hospital bed is a pale grey-white slab with a dark neutral outline all around it, which gives the sticker look. The measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 100%, so the outline is near_black rather than a tinted material tone. The mattress and frame show about 3 lightness steps, against 5-6 on the references such as the well and the stall. The surfaces are smooth with almost no grain, speckle or per-element highlights. The 10 visible tones per tile look better than they are, because the tones come mostly from the outline, the flat grey body and a few panel lines. Next to the roofed well (20 tones) and the cheese stall (17 tones), it reads as thinner, flatter and more sticker-like. Not accepted next to the references.
